bearings.paper_claim: Global balance is not significant. Best two-set partitions satisfy 0.8344 / 0.8105 / 0.7809 of edges (Epinions / Slashdot / Wikipedia), near the trivial all-positive value (about 0.80) and below degree-preserving rewired networks (0.8993 / 0.8310 / 0.8316). Sign-permuted baselines: 0.8562 / 0.7779 / 0.7866.
bearings.system_side: signed_coalitions.py partitions the member_references mention layer by frustration local search and prints F(1), F(2), F(3) against each other, with F(1) (all negatives frustrated) as the one-cluster baseline. It has no rewired or sign-permuted null, and edge direction is discarded (each edge is appended to both endpoints). Artifact 2026-07-19 signed_coalitions.json: 520 nodes, 7,153 signed edges, 5,959 positive (83.3 percent by count); F(1) 1092.31 of total |net| weight 6799.18 (16.1 percent); F(2) 15.31 percent; gap 0.76 points; 14-member splinter.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paper signs are actor-declared on web platforms; ours are LLM-valenced speech mentions weighted by |net|. Only the comparison logic transfers. Any null for the Melange layer must preserve weights as well as degrees.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 8 values and page confirmed in text. Code lines 35-36, 71-81 and 107 confirmed. Artifact counts, F(1) and F(2) percentages and the 0.76-point gap reproduced from the JSON. Minor: code line 93 prints the positive share by |net| weight, while the 83.3 figure is by edge count. Conclusion holds: no null exists in the code.

bearings.paper_claim: Global status ordering: 0.7905 / 0.8221 / 0.8538 of edges respect the best ordering, versus 0.7241 / 0.7568 / 0.7767 under sign permutation and 0.6377 / 0.6644 / 0.6321 under rewiring (random 0.50). Directed triad: a positive v-to-w-to-u path is evidence for a negative u-to-v edge, BB coefficients -0.0692 / -0.0293 / -0.0259 in the all-positive subgraph model.
bearings.paper_location: Sec 3.2 p.646 Table 5; Sec 4 p.649 Table 8
bearings.system_side: member_reference_layer.py stores directed speaker-to-target edges with net = (pos - neg) / (pos + neg + neu). signed_coalitions.py appends each edge to both endpoints, so direction is discarded before partitioning, and no ordering or directed-triad test exists on the mention layer.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Only meaningful if a negative public mention is an asymmetric judgement by the speaker about the target. Any ordering is a heuristic model output, never an influence, access or closeness claim (D-025). Dyads with edges in both directions are set aside by the paper and are not reciprocity evidence (D-104..D-108).
bearings.verifier_note: Table 8 and Table 5 values and page numbers confirmed. Code lines 35-36 confirmed to append both endpoints. Net formula confirmed at member_reference_layer.py line 372 (within the cited range). Paper codes opposite-direction pairs as 0 (Sec 3.1), so the reciprocity caveat holds. Suggestion only; the existence claim about the Melange layer is confirmed.

bearings.paper_claim: Epinions balanced-sample accuracy about 93.4 percent (6.58 percent error, All23 model, minimum embeddedness 25, 10-fold CV). Slashdot and Wikipedia accuracies appear only in plotted Figure 1, not in the text. Balanced AUC about 0.90 and full-data AUC about 0.95 (text). Wikipedia self-trained accuracy 0.8021 (Table 6). Triad features add little at low embeddedness.
bearings.paper_location: Sec 3.1 p.644 and Figure 1; Sec 3.3 p.647 Table 6
bearings.system_side: Reference-edge signs come from per-context LLM valence aggregated into net. The eyeball sheet is capped at 500 edges (member_reference_layer.py around line 392). A 2-context minimum was not confirmed in the lines read. A leave-one-out sign prediction on the mention layer would give a structural consistency check: if valence were noise, accuracy would sit near the positive base rate.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Needs an embeddedness census first: about 7,153 signed edges over 520 nodes, and many dyads may have few common neighbours, where triad features carry little information. Predictability measures consistency, not validity of the labels, and does not replace gold-label review. State the base rate and denominator with any reported accuracy.
bearings.verifier_note: The 93-94 percent figure is confirmed for Epinions only. The text gives no Slashdot or Wikipedia balanced accuracy, so a cross-site range was not established; Wikipedia is stated as clearly lower. The 500-edge cap is confirmed. The 2-context minimum was not confirmed. The leave-one-out check is an analyst suggestion, not a paper result.

bearings.paper_claim: In the undirected 4-type model, learned coefficients match balance theory for the three non-mm triad types in all three datasets. The enemy-of-enemy (mm) coefficient is negative in all three (-0.0149 Epinions, -0.0262 Slashdot, -0.0465 Wikipedia), disagreeing with balance. The authors say this is consistent with Davis weak balance, which makes no prediction for mm.
bearings.system_side: The member-relationships pilot uses shared negative targets (members whom both a and b referenced negatively) as a discovery stratum (signed_reference_proximity, sorted by shared-negative count, descending) and as a descriptive feature. A code comment states the pattern has no assumed affinity sign.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The pilot pattern is directed (a and b both point negatively at c). The paper's evidence is for the undirected collapse only; the Table 2 directed rows are hard to read in the text extraction, so no directed-level sign is claimed. The paper shows the mm pattern is not balance-like; it does not show the pattern carries no sign.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 3 coefficients and the Davis wording confirmed. Code comment and feature confirmed at run.py lines 91-93 and 160. The paper's mm coefficients are small but negative, so 'supports sign-agnostic' overstates the paper; the relation is changed to qualifies. The descending sort on shared negatives uses the pattern as an ordering key in discovery, which the comment describes as discovery-only.

bearings.paper_claim: Using all 16 signed directed triad counts (which include the 4 positive-only path types) instead of only those 4 positive-only path counts raises accuracy for predicting a positive edge on matched non-edge pairs (chance 0.50): 0.5612 to 0.5911 Epinions, 0.5579 to 0.5953 Slashdot, 0.6983 to 0.7114 Wikipedia (gains 1.3 to 3.7 points).
bearings.system_side: cosponsor_forecast.py feature list uses prior cosponsorship history, network degree and eigenvector, NOMINATE, party, state, chamber, seniority, committee terms, bill type and policy area. It has no signed or mention-derived feature. prior_sponsor_affinity is a count of prior-Congress HR/S cosponsorships with the sponsor. METHOD_NOTE confirms a fixed ridge lambda of 1.0.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Gains are 1.3 to 3.7 points on a matched-embeddedness task and may vanish against a cosponsorship-history baseline, which the forecaster must beat first. Only references dated before the forecast Congress may enter. The paper's comparison also changes feature count, so the gain is attributable to the added signed types only.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 9 values and gains confirmed. The positive-only set (4 path counts) is a subset of the 16 triads, so the comparison isolates the added signed types; the claim wording now says so. Feature list and ridge note confirmed. The 265,396 frozen-prediction count was not found in the fec/lobbying source and was not checked against any frozen artifact.

related.why: Paper does not cite Aref. It bears on the missing null: its global-balance partitions score below degree-preserving rewired networks, the baseline the Aref-Neal diagnostic currently lacks. Item exists in the vault.

Paper does not cite Aref 2020. Both use a frustration-type partition objective; this paper finds no global faction signal in three signed networks, so any partition result on signed data needs a null. Item exists in the vault.
Paper does not cite Zareie. Its Sec 5 shows signed triad features improve positive-edge existence over positive-only path features, not over unsigned similarity baselines. Item exists in the vault.

summary_issues: summary_md says about 93-94 percent balanced accuracy across the sites; the text gives this for Epinions only (6.58 percent error). Slashdot and Wikipedia accuracies appear only in plotted Figure 1, and Wikipedia is stated as clearly lower.

summary_md says learned triad coefficients agree with balance except for enemy-of-enemy; that holds only for the undirected 4-type reduction (Table 3). In the directed 16-type model (Table 2) the total-error row reads 3/3, 4/2, 7/2 (balance/status by dataset, as extracted), so balance disagrees on several directed types.

summary_md says the paper supports keeping shared-enemy counts sign-agnostic. The paper reports a small negative mm coefficient and says only that Davis weak balance makes no prediction; this supports not assuming a sign, not that the pattern carries none.
summary_md says mm matches Davis weak balance (no prediction). The paper says the disagreement is consistent with Davis weak balance; the learned mm sign is negative, so 'match' overstates it.
summary_md omits that the paper says balance alignment is notably weaker for Wikipedia (Sec 3.2, p.645). This matters because Melange votes are public-facing mentions.
The 83 percent positive figure: the artifact confirms 83.3 percent by edge count, but code line 93 prints the positive share by |net| weight. Cite count and weight separately.

Unverified in this pass: 4,358 signed reference edges in the component catalogue; the 265,396 frozen forecaster predictions (no such number in fec/lobbying source); the June Phase-2 workbook Persuadable Index use; a 2-context minimum in member_reference_layer.py; Paul's valuation of Aref-Neal, which comes from memory notes and not from this paper.
Tang 2015 related link dropped: this paper neither cites nor discusses Tang, so an extends relation is not supported by the text. The item exists, but the relation rests on outside knowledge.
ext file checked against the text: key findings and table values are accurate. Its edge-count discrepancy (841,000 in text vs 841,200 in Table 1) is already flagged there.
